observation: 16 simulated users never opened a session; median time to first session for the rest was 6.1 days.
limitation: No login/registration events; session existence is the login proxy.
product_implication: Investigate the post-registration handoff (verification, first-open prompt) and the multi-day delay to first session.

observation: Every user with a session also has feature events, but 302 individual sessions contain no events.
limitation: Zero-event sessions may be logging gaps rather than behaviour.
product_implication: Instrument session_started/feature_impression to separate empty visits from tracking loss.

stage: First feature → second distinct feature (first active day)
observation: Median distinct features on the first active day: 4.
limitation: Breadth on day 1 depends on how many events a session contains.
product_implication: Cross-feature discovery on day 1 appears high; low-breadth day-1 users are the target for discovery tests.

stage: Feature view → feature start (user×feature, Missions & Spin)
observation: Many viewers never record a start of the same feature; many starters never record a view (369 user×feature pairs).
limitation: Only 2 features log both a view and a start; views and starts are not linked within sessions (DQ-035).
product_implication: Treat as a hypothesis signal: test clearer calls-to-action on mission and spin surfaces.

observation: Every task record has a start timestamp – view→start drop-off is not observable.
limitation: Task records appear to be created only when a task is started (no pure 'viewed' records).
product_implication: Add task_viewed events independent of starts to measure task-list friction.

observation: 2051 abandoned and 1520 failed; 648 pending records excluded.
limitation: Pending tasks may later resolve; failure_reason is categorical only.
product_implication: Largest record-level friction point – investigate the dominant failure reasons by category.

stage: First meaningful activity → second meaningful activity (separate session)
observation: Share of completers who complete again in another session.
limitation: Event-based completions only (task completions excluded here to keep a single source).
product_implication: Post-completion prompts (next suggested activity) are a candidate investigation.

stage: First active day → second active day (first 30 days)
observation: Within their first 30 days, 179 of 716 users with a full 30-day horizon were active on only one day (all-time, unrestricted: 158 one-day users).
limitation: Restricted to users first active ≥30 days before data end; strongly calendar-dependent (see cohorts).
product_implication: Second-day return is a primary user-level drop-off; post-first-day re-engagement is a key investigation area.

stage: Second active day → third active day (first 30 days)
observation: Share of returning users who return a second time within 30 days.
product_implication: Habit-formation mechanics (streaks, daily rewards) are candidates for investigation here.

stage: Third active day → seventh active day (first 30 days)
observation: Progression to a 7th active day within the first 30 days.
product_implication: Mid-term progression: missions/levels may matter more than onboarding here (hypothesis).

observation: Users with ≥30 observable days who were active again between day 7 and day 30.
limitation: Restricted to users first active ≥30 days before data end.
product_implication: Week-2+ re-engagement is the target for notification-timing experiments.
